question: Can discrete causal-law disagreement scheduling with guaranteed prior minimum exploration improve action-consequence learning efficiency over fully trained uniform, random and strong conventional active/family-aware controls on nine fresh synthetic causal worlds?

worlds.generation: F47 SHA256 first8 namespace F47/{degree,edge,sign}/v1 selects unknown directed signed graph with degree from options, no self edges. F47/obs/v1 hash gives public binary observed target vector after action0/1: p=1/4 baseline and 7/8 for preferred action. True graph and law family evaluator-only.
worlds.budget_formula: exactly 2*N*b paired actions (two public source interventions per pair) at each checkpoint, high first in reporting. Each intervention sees a full N-target public binary outcome vector; max 48 paired observations in each (source,context) row. No free observations.

methods.native: Reuse F46 isolated LocalLearner signed int16 local plasticity without model-source changes or tuning; direct signed cutoff 0.45 contrast, restore exact checkpoint.
methods.tournament: Before allocation, collect 4 paired action observations on EVERY source/context row, lowest row first. From then on select via deterministic qualitative causal-law disagreement votes: for each target examine context0/1 signed effect classifications at threshold 0.45; derive best fitting among invariant [1,1], gated [0,1], and flipped [1,-1] by minimum squared deviation of observed contrasts (equal to categorical hypothesis tournament, not F46 magnitude-near-threshold score); each target whose sign pattern disagrees with that hypothesis votes for further observations of the discrepant context row, weighted by count 1/(1+row count). Rank rows by sum of votes; ties lowest row. Categorical sign mismatch is the ranking signal, not continuous proximity to 0.45.
methods.row_caps: Prefix schedule hard cap per row: 12 paired samples until smallest b=6 budget (12*N total pairs); 24 until b=12 (24*N pairs); 48 until b=24 (48*N pairs). 4-pair mandatory exploration in each 2*N rows occurs before every budget. Never rearrange outcome histories in low-budget reporting.
methods.uniform: F46 local learner + round robin paired row selection.
methods.random: F46 local learner + separately seeded deterministic random selection among rows under cap.
methods.conventional_active: F46 independent Bernoulli MLE uncertainty active row-selection and F46 weighted family-aware least-squares predictions; same interventions budget but selection-dependent outcomes.
methods.control: For each history, exact independent fitted MLE parity with local weights. Strongest control = max direct F1 of conventional-active family WLS, uniform family WLS, uniform independent fitted MLE. No hidden true graph or true family supplied to any mechanism.
methods.score: Direct signed precision/recall/F1 over all context/source/nonself-target candidates. Two-hop unique signed path F1 with true ambiguous paths excluded, identical scorer for all models.
methods.negative: Action0-only abstention, wrong-source permutation lowers development F1, tampered cold checkpoint rejected, bit-exact cold restore, additional real isolated paired action on copy does not change another learned source row.
methods.cost: Report action count, outcomes bits, code/learned weights and checkpoint bytes, runtime by policy. Equal action counts are NOT full compute equivalence.

decision: DEV_TOURNAMENT_ACTIVE_POLICY_GO only if every frozen gate passes; otherwise DEV_TOURNAMENT_ACTIVE_POLICY_NO_GO. Do not retune policy, outcomes, budgets, thresholds, seeds or scripts after results. Strong conventional may win; report it transparently. SCIENTIFIC_PASS always false: source-free predeclared synthetic DEV, not novel worlds or matched compute.
